name: LinkedIn: Company Jobs
summary: Open a company's LinkedIn Jobs tab, follow its own Show all jobs link, and return the open roles plus a hiring-location breakdown.
description: Open a LinkedIn company page's Jobs tab, click the page's own Show all jobs link into the company-filtered jobs search, set the location filter through the real search box, and return the open roles. Each role carries job_id, title, company, location, workplace type (Remote / Hybrid / On-site), how long ago it was posted, and the canonical /jobs/view/ URL. Also returns the total result count LinkedIn reports and a hiring_locations tally built from the returned cards, which answers where the company is currently hiring. Read-only: never clicks Apply, Easy Apply, or Save.

company.description: A LinkedIn company slug (e.g. stripe) OR a full https://www.linkedin.com/company/<slug>/ URL.

location.description: Location filter typed into the jobs search box (e.g. Bengaluru, United States). Defaults to Worldwide.

max_jobs.description: Maximum number of job cards to return. Defaults to 25. Hard cap 50.

steps.name: Extract job cards and aggregate the hiring locations

help.summary: Return a company's open LinkedIn roles plus a tally of where it is hiring.

parameters.company: A LinkedIn company slug (e.g. stripe) OR a full /company/<slug>/ URL.
parameters.location: Location typed into the jobs search box. Defaults to Worldwide.
parameters.max_jobs: Maximum job cards to return (default 25, cap 50).

examples.description: Return Stripe's open roles worldwide with a hiring-location tally.

examples.command: rzn-browser run linkedin company-jobs --param company="stripe" --param location="Bengaluru" --param max_jobs=50
examples.description: Same, narrowed to Bengaluru, returning up to 50 roles.

returns: { slug, company_id, search_url, location_filter, total_results, jobs_returned, hiring_locations[], jobs[] }
hiring_locations entries are formatted "<location> — <n> of <jobs_returned>", so they describe the returned sample, not LinkedIn's full index.
notes: Read-only. Never clicks Apply, Easy Apply, Save, or Set alert.

The company id is read from the company page's own Show all jobs link, then the run opens /jobs/search/?f_C=<id>. That link's native target is /jobs/search-results/, which renders without a search box, and clicking it is intercepted by LinkedIn's own router, so the workflow navigates to the equivalent /jobs/search/ page instead. That is one page load per run, not a reload loop.

The location filter is typed into LinkedIn's real search box rather than pushed through a query string, because LinkedIn pre-fills the box from your session region and a bare f_C URL silently keeps that region.
total_results is LinkedIn's own count and saturates at "1,000+". jobs_returned is what was actually scraped.
The jobs search list is the classic UI, so li[data-occludable-job-id] and the artdeco lockup selectors are stable, unlike the hashed SDUI class names elsewhere on LinkedIn.

Job cards are virtualised: an off-screen card keeps its id but loses its title and location. The extractor therefore scrolls the results pane itself and harvests on every tick, and pages forward with the View next page button, rather than scrolling first and reading once.
Every execute_javascript step sets use_cdp_eval because LinkedIn's CSP blocks script-tag injection on all pages.
Use linkedin_job_detail with a returned job_id for the full description of one role.
